origin: cwe/78/python Key Principles: ['tar', 'czf', archive, filename] with a filename of '--to-command=...' hands tar an option and no shell was involved

finding.name: OS Command Injection
finding.summary: create_backup_archive already avoids a shell (shell=False, an argument list), so no shell metacharacter can inject a second command - but filenames is attacker-controlled and appended directly as tar arguments with no check for a leading '-'. A filenames entry such as --absolute-names is parsed by tar as an option rather than a file to archive, silently changing tar's behaviour for every filename that follows it in the same invocation.

trap: Confirming shell=False and an argument list are already in place (they are) or adding a check for shell metacharacters in each filename closes command injection but does nothing about this finding: tar parses its own argument list independently of the shell, and an argument beginning with - is read as an option regardless of how the process was spawned. The fix has to reject any filenames entry that starts with -, or insert a literal -- into the command list before the user-controlled filenames so tar stops parsing options at that point (['tar', 'czf', archive_path, '--'] + filenames).
must_preserve: create_backup_archive still archives every filenames entry that does not start with -. Any entry beginning with - is either rejected outright or passed through as a literal filename via the -- separator, never interpreted as a tar option.
